new_entities.name: Systemic treatment for presumed Candida overgrowth
new_entities.description: Systemic antifungal-style treatment or anti-Candida protocols used for presumed intestinal Candida overgrowth or Candida-related nonspecific symptom syndromes.

new_entities.name: Symptom resolution
new_entities.description: Substantial improvement or disappearance of symptomatic complaints attributed to an exposure or treatment.

edges.effect_quant: A 2002 systematic review of 96 citations on intestinal Candida colonization found no evidence that most commonly blamed lifestyle or medication exposures predispose immunocompetent adults to clinically meaningful gut-Candida syndromes, and it concluded that therapeutic studies did not substantiate a broad Candida-syndrome model.
edges.population: immunocompetent adults with presumed intestinal Candida overgrowth or nonspecific symptom complexes attributed to gut Candida
edges.mechanism: Candida can colonize the gastrointestinal tract as a commensal or pathobiont, but colonization alone does not prove that nonspecific systemic symptoms are being driven by fungal overgrowth or that empiric systemic treatment will resolve them.
edges.summary: This is best treated as a contested or largely unsupported functional-medicine claim rather than a validated therapeutic pathway. Human review literature does not show a clear, reproducible syndrome in which systemic anti-Candida treatment reliably resolves broad nonspecific symptoms in otherwise immunocompetent adults.
edges.caveats: This edge does not apply to invasive candidiasis or clearly diagnosed mucosal fungal infections. It is specifically about the broad 'Candida overgrowth' explanation for diffuse symptoms and the claim that systemic treatment predictably fixes them.
